Class SovereignTreasuryBondEngine

All Implemented Interfaces:

public class SovereignTreasuryBondEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine

Sovereign Treasury, Public Debt & Coinage Debasement Engine

Models the macroscopic budgetary, fiscal, and debt dynamics of sovereign polities. Replaces synthetic debt and currency debasement sigmoids with an authentic double-entry state balance sheet (tax extraction, military expenditures, treasury bullion reserves, bond market credit issuance, and crisis debasement).

Scientific Foundations

  • P. G. M. Dickson (1967) The Financial Revolution in England: A Study in the Development of Public Credit 1688–1756, Macmillan.
  • Carmen M. Reinhart & Kenneth S. Rogoff (2009) This Time Is Different: Eight Centuries of Financial Folly, Princeton University Press.
  • David Stasavage (2011) States of Credit: Size, Power, and the Development of European Polities, Princeton University Press.
  • Kevin Butcher & Matthew Ponting (2014) The Metallurgy of Roman Silver Coinage: From the Reform of Nero to the Reform of Trajan, Cambridge University Press.

Mechanistic Dynamics

The sovereign state levies taxes on domestic agricultural surplus and commercial transit tolls: $$\text{Revenue} = \tau_{\text{tax}} \cdot (Y_{\text{agr}} + Y_{\text{trade}})$$ State expenditures are driven by standing military upkeep, bureaucratic administration, and wars: $$\text{Expenditure} = N_{\text{military}} \cdot w_{\text{soldier}} + \text{Bureaucracy} + \text{WarCrisisCost}$$ When $\text{Expenditure} > \text{Revenue}$, the fiscal deficit is covered first by drawing down precious metal bullion reserves in the state treasury. If bullion is depleted:

  1. In regimes without public credit markets (Antiquity, feudal monarchies), the sovereign debases the coin purity: $$\Delta \text{Purity} = -\frac{\text{Deficit}}{\text{Total Coinage Issued}}$$
  2. In regimes with institutional representative bond markets (Italian city-states, Dutch Republic, Bank of England), the state issues sovereign debt securities: $$\text{Debt}_{t+1} = \text{Debt}_t \cdot (1 + r) + \text{Deficit}_t$$
